new_statements.citation: one of the works listed for this language (see the verification note)
new_statements.check: reported on verification, not yet confirmed
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work is listed for this item and the compiler opened it, so the spot-check was run on the earlier-pass silent works already saved in the same directory. Tryon 2010 (printed p. 88 = pdf page 306): only the list entry '7. Kula: Wusi, Kerepua, Elia 1 [350]' and a note on four extinct languages of the Wusi area; zero stress/accent hits on that page. Tryon 1976 : the single 'stressed syllables' line in the whole file is footnote 10 to the POC consonant-correspondence table ('*p becomes y in stressed syllables, /ɣ/ elsewhere') and it is attached to row 64 Sakau, not to the Wusi rows 38-40. Taman, Taman & Rangelov 2025 (Te Reo 68(2)): 'stress' appears only as 'we also stress how important…

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir & Eleanor Ridge. 2025. VanBib: A database of references to resources on Vanuatu languages, v1.3. Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17628152
sources.note: Bibliographic check: the 13 entries tagged wusi1237 are all wordlists (Tryon 1976, ABVD, ASJP, kava/taro/food-plant name lists 1988/1998/2004, Vanuatu Voices 2025) or overviews (Tryon 2010); no grammar, sketch or phonology is recorded for the language.

sources.citation: Lynch, John, Malcolm Ross & Terry Crowley. 2002. The Oceanic languages. (Curzon Language Family Series.) Richmond: Curzon. xxii+924 pp. ('Sakao' grammar sketch adapted by Terry Crowley from Guy, pp. 599-607; appendix language listing p. 886.)
sources.note: listing only ('Southwest Santo f.: Wusi, Akei, Malmariv (Tiale), Navut'), no source; no phonology.

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir. 2026 (in press). The phonological history of 17 varieties in western Espiritu Santo (Vanuatu). Language and Linguistics in Melanesia (vol. 44?).
sources.note: First phonological treatment ever of Wusi (09_Wusi_Kula) and Kerepua (08_Kerepua_Tuijo); may contain synchronic inventories and a prosody remark. Supplementary data already posted 2026-09-15; article not yet on langlxmelanesia.com as of 2026-09-17 (open access when it appears).
sources.venue: The phonological history of 17 varieties in western Espiritu Santo (Vanuatu)

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir. 2026. Supplementary materials to 'The phonological history of 17 varieties in western Espiritu Santo (Vanuatu)', Language and Linguistics in Melanesia. Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.22762181 (methods PDF + ODS lexical dataset incl. columns 08_Kerepua_Tuijo, 09_Wusi_Kula).
sources.note: Nothing; 'relatively broad IPA transcription.. Other finer phonetic detail has generally been ignored'; only 4 stress marks in 8615 datapoints, none in the Wusi/Kerepua columns. The article itself is not yet online (LLM vol. 44 page checked).

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir, Eleanor Ridge & Lana Takau. 2025. Linguistics in Vanuatu 45 years after Independence. Te Reo 68(2) (Special issue 'Vanuatu languages in context', ed. T. Rangelov, E. Ridge, L. Takau & V. Chen): 31-78. Wellington: Linguistic Society of New Zealand.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content for any language. For wusi1237 the Appendix (pp. 77-78) records: '24 Tuijo-Kula wusi1237 No grammar | Short list | research score 0.0 | No corpus | No Bible' -- i.e. the authors (Dec 2025) know of no grammatical description at all; sec. 6.1 only remarks generically that audio corpora 'provide phonetic and prosodic detail'. Confirms independently that no source stating Wusi stress/tone exists as of late 2025.

sources.citation: Takau, Lana et al. 2025. Vanuatu Voices v1.4, doculects Wusi (Kula), Kerepua (Tuijo), Elia: audio wordlists (282 items each).
sources.note: Open audio for every item; stress could be determined instrumentally; transcriptions downloaded now carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: Takau, Lana et al. 2025. Vanuatu Voices v1.4: Wordlist for Wusi (language Kula), 282 items with audio. Leipzig: MPI-EVA. doi:10.5281/zenodo.17407434;https://vanuatuvoices.clld.org/contributions/Wusi
sources.note: No statement; IPA transcriptions carry no stress marks (vowel length is marked, often on the penult, e.g. liːma 'five', βaːti 'four', raptoːlu 'eight', but that is data, not a description). Audio is open and would permit a first-hand determination.

sources.citation: Taman, Allan, Sabrina Taman & Tihomir Rangelov. 2025. Language ecosystems in Western Santo. Te Reo 68(2): 186-245 (special issue 'Vanuatu languages in context'). doi:10.5281/zenodo.18723279
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic/vitality survey with a section on Tuijo/Kula (wusi1237, ~401 L1 speakers); states 'Linguistic data from this part of Vanuatu are scarce' and that the language lacks literacy materials and a writing system.

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir. 2022. The languages of Santo and the Vanuatu Voices database. Talk in the Friends of the Museum series, National Museum of Vanuatu, Port Vila, 6 December 2022. Slides (PDF, 30 MB), MPG PuRe item_3492326.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content for Wusi/Kerepua: village populations, migration from the hills c. 1950, 'same language as in Kerepua (a few lexical differences)', comprehension of neighbouring lects, one caption 'Wusi claypots uro tano'. The only phonological remark in the deck concerns Nokuku ('expanded vowel system + final vowel loss').
sources.venue: Talk in the Friends of the Museum series, National Museum of Vanuatu, Port Vila, 6 December

sources.citation: Lynch, John. 2019. The bilabial-to-linguolabial shift in Southern Oceanic: a subgrouping diagnostic? Oceanic Linguistics 58(2): 292-323.
sources.note: Only other modern phonological paper Glottolog attaches to wusi1237; low chance of a stress remark on West Santo languages but unchecked.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell. 2010. The languages of Espiritu Santo, Vanuatu. In Bowden, Himmelmann & Ross (eds), A journey through Austronesian and Papuan linguistic and cultural space: papers in honour of Andrew K. Pawley, 283-290. Pacific Linguistics 615.
sources.note: Nothing; lists '7. Kula: Wusi, Kerepua, Elia 1 [350]' with village/speaker info only.

sources.citation: Clark, Ross. 2009. *Leo Tuai: A comparative lexical study of North and Central Vanuatu languages. Pacific Linguistics 603.
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 C59 2009
sources.note: Gives stress notes only for its principal witness languages (Nokuku, Kiai, Tamabo, Araki, Raga etc.); Wusi appears only as cited forms in cognate sets; no Wusi stress statement. General remark that PNCV stress was probably penultimate (sec. 2.1.3).

sources.citation: Lynch, John & Terry Crowley. 2001. Languages of Vanuatu: a new survey and bibliography. Pacific Linguistics 517. Canberra: ANU. Sec. 3.3.8 'Wusi', p. 51.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 L96 2001)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 L96 2001
sources.note: Nothing; states 'The only other published information from this language apart from these wordlists [Tryon 1976] are several names for kava varieties'; summary table rates Wusi grammar 0, dictionary no, texts no.

sources.citation: Clark, Ross. 1985. Languages of north and central Vanuatu: groups, chains, clusters and waves. In Andrew Pawley & Lois Carrington (eds), Austronesian linguistics at the 15th Pacific Science Congress, 199-236. Pacific Linguistics C-88. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Only segmental history: table p. 207 gives Wusi '±' for the *ng > n merger (no entry for *d/*q), and p. ~222 notes Wusi and Malo lost dual/trial independent pronouns. The words stress/accent/penultimate do not occur anywhere in the paper.
sources.venue: Austronesian linguistics at the 15th Pacific Science Congress

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. 1978. The languages of the New Hebrides: internal and external relationships. In S. A. Wurm & Lois Carrington (eds), Second International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics: Proceedings, fascicle 2, 877-902. Pacific Linguistics C-61. Canberra: ANU. (hdl 1885/253239)
sources.note: Nothing on prosody anywhere; subgrouping argued from lexicostatistics and consonant sound correspondences ('the phonological evidence.. suggests', pp. ~888-892) at subgroup level; Wusi is only a name in Chart I (p. 880). stress/accent/tone/penult: zero hits.
sources.venue: Second International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics: Proceedings, fascicle 2

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. 1976. New Hebrides languages: an internal classification. Pacific Linguistics C-50. Canberra: ANU.
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number PL6211.N44 T7
sources.note: Nothing for Wusi: wordlists (38 Wusi I, 39 Wusi II, 40 Kerepua, 45 Nonona) and sound-correspondence tables only; no per-language prosody; the words 'penultimate'/'accent' do not occur in the volume.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. 1972. The languages of the New Hebrides: a checklist and general survey. In C. Beaumont, D. Tryon & S. A. Wurm (eds), Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia No. 3, 43-84. Pacific Linguistics A-35. Canberra: ANU. (hdl 1885/254325)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content: per-language checklist (location, villages, population, alternative names), a tentative lexicostatistical classification (sec. 3.0, 'based on sample lexicostatistical comparisons and upon grammatical and phonological features known to the writer' -- features not given) and comparative wordlist tables in which Wusi appears as a column. The words stress/accent/tone/penultimate do not occur ('stressed' once, in the sense 'emphasised').
sources.venue: Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia No. 3
